picks.desc: Mesh short-sleeve in the Oaklawn cut — the piece that shows the Publish pattern-making most clearly. Falls like a skate tee, breathes like golf kit.
The Caddie quarter-zip in black. Boxy through the body, short in the sleeve, no branding beyond a small chest mark. Wears as easily over jeans.
Marbled anorak, the loudest thing in the current range and the one that will date the best. Pull-on, hood, half-zip.
This washed grey crew carries the Malbon Ironworks division print. It is the nearest the 2026 range gets to the graphic energy the brand was built on.
From the Sungjae Im line — navy, heavyweight, tour-athlete branding done straight. The clearest signal of where Malbon has moved.
Reversible in military green. Outerwear at $348 is the part of the business the new money is aimed at.
3M-treated athletic tee in the LIV colourway. Reflective hit, oversized body — the entry point to the brand.
Open Terrain hood in black with the outline graphic across the chest. Heavyweight, boxy, the piece that sells out first.
PlutoDry Target jacket in steel blue, panelled and cut wide. Technical fabric doing a streetwear silhouette rather than the reverse.
